label: rem:q-casimir-remark
title: Normalisation and role of the $q$-Casimir element
html:
The q-Casimir element is the distinguished central element of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) whose eigenvalue on the spin-j irreducible encodes the categorical q-angular momentum. Subtracting (q + q^{-1}) in the numerator ensures the eigenvalue vanishes on the trivial representation and has a finite classical limit. Equivalently,

  C_q  =  E F  +  \frac{q^{-1}\,K + q\,K^{-1} - (q + q^{-1})}
                        {(q - q^{-1})^2}.

By existence, C_q is central and acts on the (2j+1)-dimensional highest-weight module V_j as the scalar [j]_q\,[j+1]_q, where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}). Centrality makes C_q an endomorphism of the identity functor on \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)), the categorical counterpart of the angular-momentum-squared operator.
